minutes.headline: Town Meeting rejected new authority to amend the capital plan, but approved Marshall Park engineering funding.
minutes.summary: This special town meeting acted on 15 warrant articles: it approved FY23 budget adjustments, a police union contract's first-year funding, $184,000 for Marshall Park engineering (to support up to $2 million in outside grants), a firefighter/reserve-officer retirement buyback provision, and a motel zoning change and a citizen-petitioned rezoning. It rejected giving town meeting authority to amend individual capital plan line items, rejected overriding the APDC's denial of Ritter Library window replacement, rejected changes to the APDC's own review bylaw, and rejected moving the annual town meeting and election from May to April.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting rejected giving itself authority to amend individual line items in the capital plan.
It approved a transfer for final engineering and design at Marshall Park, meant to support outside grant applications.
It approved FY23 budget adjustments to town management, assessors, planning board and facilities and grounds lines.
It approved year-one funding for the new police officers' collective bargaining agreement.
It rejected overriding the APDC's denial of Ritter Library window replacement and rejected changing the APDC's own review bylaw.

why_it_matters: The capital plan vote leaves individual project funding outside town meeting's amending power unless a future warrant article changes the bylaw again.
Marshall Park funding lets the town move ahead on grant applications that the project depends on to cover a large share of its cost.
The Ritter Library and APDC bylaw votes leave the historic commission's review process and the library's window question unresolved.
